definitions.explanation: A marked section of road where pedestrians have the right of way to cross safely, typically indicated by white stripes on the pavement.

examples.japanese: {横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}るときは{左右|さゆう}を{確認|かくにん}しましょう。
examples.english: Check both ways when crossing at the crosswalk.

examples.japanese: {横断歩道|おうだんほどう}の{手前|てまえ}で{車|くるま}が{止|と}まった。
examples.english: The car stopped in front of the crosswalk.

examples.japanese: {信号|しんごう}のない{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}では{歩行者|ほこうしゃ}{優先|ゆうせん}です。
examples.english: At crosswalks without traffic lights, pedestrians have priority.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}り{終|お}わるまで{車|くるま}は{待|ま}っていた。
examples.english: The cars waited until the children finished crossing the crosswalk.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}の{前|まえ}の{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}には{毎朝|まいあさ}ボランティアの{人|ひと}が{立|た}って{子|こ}どもたちの{安全|あんぜん}を{見守|みまも}っている。
examples.english: Every morning, volunteers stand at the crosswalk in front of the school to watch over the children's safety.

notes:
COMPONENTS:
・{横断|おうだん} (crossing) + {歩道|ほどう} (sidewalk, footpath)

TRAFFIC RULES IN JAPAN: Drivers are legally required to stop for pedestrians waiting at crosswalks, even without traffic signals. The {道路交通法|どうろこうつうほう} (Road Traffic Act) mandates this, though compliance rates vary by region.

RELATED TERMS:
・{歩行者|ほこうしゃ} (pedestrian)
・{信号機|しんごうき} (traffic light)
・{歩道橋|ほどうきょう} (pedestrian overpass)
・{地下道|ちかどう} (underground passage)
・{踏切|ふみきり} (railroad crossing)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}る (to cross at the crosswalk)
・{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}の{白線|はくせん} (white lines of the crosswalk)
